about: Generated by scripts/benchmarks.ts from the published results of idtrack-reproducibility at the commit: do not edit.

tree.name: main
tree.what: idtrack's main at the release, whose answers are those of the release 0.1.2 (`7f71b26`: documentation strings only); asked on `r2`'s graph files, which its own builder rebuilt with the same content digests (`[graphs.main]`)

truth: Every expected answer is read from Ensembl's own files or from the authorities (HGNC, MGI, VGNC, NCBI, UniProt, ...), never from idtrack.
historyCaveat: The history truth is Ensembl's `stable_id_event`, the same table idtrack stores (read by independent code, and checked against REST for a sample): it tests idtrack's use of the history, not the history.

intervals.cluster: where one id or one lineage gives many queries (A, A*, the travel strata of B, C at many releases): resampling the unit that generated the queries, 2,000 resamples, seed 20261118.

judges.decided: the base set with its revision set `<set>_dec`, which holds only the lines whose expectation a decided rule changes
judges.when: a rule of idtrack is decided but not yet built

families.title: D, real-world inputs
families.measures: an atlas project's feature lists, source inference, marker lists, mixed lists, judged by locus

items.text: the feature's gene model in Ensembl's GTF of R against the models of every gene of 115 (main GTF) by exon bases shared on the strand.
per release r of the window, the distinct items of the list that are genes of r on the assembly that serves r.

the genes whose GTF display name the symbol is at the release read (primary region; exactly, else without letter case), walked to 115 by the strict walk with living ids; without a release, read as rule `start_release` reads it.

each item is a published line of the accuracy harness (the latest line of its qid, the corrected judge) asked without a release to 115, and keeps that line's truth whole, so F0's scorer judges the item exactly as the harness judges the single call.

families.title: B, names over time
families.measures: display names, symbols of the authorities, aliases and their forms at every release (exhaustive on `main` in the five organisms; on `d4c2dda` in rhesus and cynomolgus)

truth.opening: Nothing of idtrack; every file is in its organism's `SOURCES.tsv`.

items.text: the GTF's `gene_name` of every release of the window (pig 56 to 115, human, mouse and rhesus 48 to 115, cynomolgus 91 to 115), with the region where the release's GTF marks patches (human and mouse from 82): copies on patches are reported apart.

where an archive BioMart answers, its HGNC, MGI, UniProt gene name, NCBI label and WikiGene tables, VGNC's symbol of BioMart's VGNC id and the Vega names, as the accuracy harness reads them; and at every release Ensembl's cross-references of the release: the labels of HGNC, MGI, VGNC, UniProt gene name, NCBI gene, WikiGene, Vega and the clone-based names.

BioMart's synonym table where an archive answers (it holds the synonyms of a gene's display cross-reference only), and Ensembl's synonyms of every cross-reference where `core_synonyms/<R>.tsv.gz` is fetched.
where the synonyms of R are not read, the genes that carry the string as a synonym at any release read; where no name source of R is read, the genes that carry it as a name at any release.

A*'s walks: the strict walk with living ids is `expect`, the broad walk with ids brought back goes into `broad`; where the history ends for a name of one gene, the locus rule with the corrected judge's places across assemblies, assembly exceptions and core places; one gene that split is judged `set`; mouse display names that are projected HGNC symbols and no name in another source are left out.

each gene's display cross-reference of every release as the release's core database holds it: the name, the gene and the database it is filed under; Ensembl's GTF writes this label as `gene_name`, and the two differ at a few releases only: mouse 49, where the GTF writes the MGI accession of 21,182 genes for their symbol; release 78 of pig, mouse and human, where the label of a UniProt gene name ends in a stray `;` the GTF leaves out (418, 13, 26 genes); human 50, where the GTF adds a `.` to 412 HGNC projections; and where a GTF writes no name or an older one (cynomolgus 108: 15,619 genes; cynomolgus 112: 120; pig 105: 405; mouse 103 and 105: 24).

HGNC's complete set and withdrawn list; MGI's `MRK_List1.rpt` (withdrawn symbols with their current marker, synonyms) and `MRK_ENSEMBL.rpt` (MGI's own Ensembl ids); VGNC's gene sets; NCBI's `gene_info`.

families.title: C, external identifiers
families.measures: NCBI gene, RefSeq, UniProt and other databases' identifiers to genes and back, at every release, against Ensembl's and the databases' own tables (exhaustive on `main` in the five organisms; on `d4c2dda` in pig, rhesus and cynomolgus)

items.text: the extract of each release's MySQL dumps: one row per Ensembl object and cross-reference of C's databases, with its gene, `db_name`, `db_display_name`, accession, label, version and info type.

which of the graph's databases the reference tree's externals configuration includes at which release (by the assembly of the release's GTF) and from which object form, read from the configured `d4c2dda` checkout, with `d4c2dda`'s naming.
family A's `GenA`.

NCBI's `gene2ensembl`, `gene2refseq`, `gene_history`; RefSeq's catalog; UniProt's `idmapping_selected`, secondary and deleted accessions, isoforms; RFAM's family list; RNAcentral's mappings; miRBase's genome and sequence files; CCDS's sequence table; VGNC's gene sets.

BioMart agrees with the core reading at every archive release and database read, except release 75's Swiss-Prot table, which holds entry names where the core holds accessions (pig 566, rhesus 171, mouse 15,301, human 19,095 values); the FTP `tsv/` tables agree with it except at one release per organism (cynomolgus and rhesus 112, pig 105, mouse 103), where they lack values the core holds and pig's holds 217 RefSeq peptides the core does not, and mouse's 103 gives 2 NCBI ids one gene where the core gives two; human's NCBI ids of 87 to 116 (675 to 1,348 values per release, BioMart's tables of 105, 110, 115 and 116 alike) differ from the core reading only by the LRG records the core lists beside the Ensembl gene, which no GTF holds and the truth leaves out.

families.title: A, history travel
families.measures: history travel exhaustive over every id and release, and the graph's fidelity to Ensembl's tables (A0)

truth.opening: Nothing of idtrack. A imports A*'s truth and never copies it, so a correction of that truth reaches A as a revision set: the strict walk with living ids, sessions placed where their effect appears; the broad walk with returned ids; copies on haplotypes, patches and alternative loci reported apart; the locus rule, with places projected through Ensembl's assembly exceptions and mapped across assemblies by the chain files; the core genes the GTF lacks (human 48 to 51, cynomolgus 112).

families.title: A*, the hardest lineages
families.measures: history travel for the ids whose lineages are hardest, every origin to every target

truth.opening: Nothing of idtrack: the truth is the harness's reading of Ensembl's history through `astar/truth.py` and `astar/gen.py`.

items.lead: the strict walk with living ids
items.text: the genes the history carries the id to at the target, where an id present in the GTFs on both sides of a session is kept; sessions are crossed where their effect appears in the GTFs, not at their recorded old release; a step between the mitochondrial genome and a nuclear sequence is not followed, also where the id stays the same.

items.lead: the broad walk with returned ids
items.text: also the genes reached through ids that Ensembl retired and brought back; an answer in `broad` but not in `expect` is undetermined.

genes on haplotypes, patches and alternative loci are expected in the list idtrack reports apart; before release 82, where the GTFs label every gene `primary`, the copies are read from Ensembl's assembly exceptions.

where the history reaches nothing, an answer at the old place is undetermined and one elsewhere wrong; places on haplotypes, patches and the Y pseudoautosomal regions are projected onto the reference through Ensembl's assembly exceptions and the GRC's alignments, and mapped across assemblies by Ensembl's chain files.
the core genes of human 48 to 51 and cynomolgus 112 are present (from Ensembl's core gene tables), compared by stable id where the GTF writes no versions, and placed by the core.

families.title: E, robustness
families.measures: missing values, malformed strings, types, other organisms' ids, arguments, budgets, determinism and concurrency, metamorphic relations, the web layer

truth.opening: Nothing of idtrack. The made-unique forms are read against every release's names too: the core cross-references and the GTF of each release; synonyms only where the truth holds them (BioMart's synonym tables, the core synonym extract of 115), recorded on each such line.

tools.title: G, other tools
tools.measures: the tools people use for the same questions (Ensembl REST, BioMart, g:Profiler, MyGene.info, HGNC, UniProt, BridgeDb, pyensembl, Bioconductor's annotation packages, ...) asked the same lines, judged by the same truth and scorer from their stored responses, every disagreement with idtrack sampled and read; its published numbers (`results/g/main/all/`) rest on the scored folders `results.toml` registers per subject and reading of the input, made by `families.g.score` from the store of fetched responses (`families/g/raw/`, never fetched again; its manifest checked), on G's published sets and the families' truth, and the reading's numbers on its seeded sample

tasks.a: an old Ensembl id to its gene at 115
tasks.b: an Ensembl id at its own release
tasks.d: a previous symbol, alias or synonym

tools.reading: Only Ensembl REST (`archive/id`) and idtrack pose task a (an old Ensembl id to its gene at 115), 44 to 50 % of the web lines. On symbols (task c), aliases (d) and external identifiers (e) no tool's rate reaches idtrack's on the same kept lines in any organism; on Ensembl ids of 115 (task b) most tools and idtrack are right on every line. The rule of equal truth leaves out at most 4.3 % of a tool's posed lines (BridgeDb at 111; NCBI's files 2.7 %, every other tool 2 % or less). What a tool's wrong lines are: most are questions the tool does not claim to answer, and the rates are not a ranking of the tools' quality on the questions they claim.
tools.viewAll: the tool's answer is exactly the truth's genes
